adapter.scope: Independent reproduction of jurisdiction capability fail-closed behavior and Tari/XMR jurisdictionGate wiring at the exact closed/unmerged contributor commit.

steps: Use the clean MyZubster verification checkout, not /root/myzubster.
Run the existing Shweta verifier, which clones the public fork into a temporary directory and checks out the exact pinned commit.
Verify JavaScript syntax for the five bounded files.
Execute deterministic policy checks for GLOBAL, HK, CN_MAINLAND, unknown jurisdiction and unknown capability.
Inspect bounded Tari/XMR jurisdictionGate wiring and the middleware 403/JURISDICTION_POLICY_DENIED deny path.
Capture the verifier JSON result without credentials, tokens or private data.
cleanup: Allow the verifier TemporaryDirectory to remove the cloned fork automatically.
Do not modify, restart or reconfigure production services.
Retain only sanitized verifier output and canonical commit references.

checks: All five JavaScript syntax checks pass.
Known capabilities are allowed in GLOBAL and HK.
Tested capabilities are denied in CN_MAINLAND.
Tari wallet transfer and external settlement routes are guarded by jurisdictionGate.
XMR wallet transfer and external settlement routes are guarded by jurisdictionGate.
Deny middleware contains HTTP 403 behavior and JURISDICTION_POLICY_DENIED.
Verifier exits zero and reports status TESTED.

result.summary: Frozen and ready for an independent VPS rerun of the existing Shweta MyZubsterGateway jurisdiction-capability verifier.

limitations: The upstream pull request is closed and was not merged.
A passing checkpoint does not establish production deployment.
A passing checkpoint does not establish legal or regulatory compliance.
A passing checkpoint does not establish a security certification or audit.
The checkpoint is bounded to the exact pinned contributor commit and listed verifier behavior.
